10.1002_aenm.71552: While perovskites have emerged as frontrunners in optoelectronics due to their exceptional properties, their performance remains bottlenecked by film imperfections such as interfacial defects, non‐uniform crystallization, and band alignment mismatches. Conventional treatments often fail to simultaneously address issues at the top surface, the bulk, and the buried interface. In this work, we introduce a holistic top‐to‐bottom restructuring strategy using a facile vapor‐phase post‐treatment. This approach induces a gradient‐distributed 2D perovskite phase that extends from the surface into the bulk while uniquely healing structural voids and chemical inhomogeneities at the buried interface. This synergistic restructuring optimizes the energy band structure for accelerated carrier extraction and passivates defects throughout the entire film depth. As a result, our unencapsulated n‐i‐p solar cells demonstrate exceptional environmental resilience, maintaining over 90% of their initial efficiency after 2,800 h of high‐humidity exposure. This study establishes a new benchmark for stability and provides a robust pathway for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.
10.1002_anie.3251724: Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage owing to their intrinsic safety. However, their lifespan is severely limited by side reactions such as dendrite growth and hydrogen evolution at the Zn‐electrolyte interface. Conventional single‐electrolyte‐additive approaches are thermodynamically constrained, yielding only insufficient coverage of the inner‐Helmholtz plane (IHP) and poor control of interfacial reactions. Here, we report an interfacial fluorinated‐ion crowding strategy by simultaneously introducing multiple low‐concentration fluorinated additives. Computational and spectroscopic analyses reveal that various‐sized F‐groups densely occupy the IHP, displacing water molecules and homogenizing Zn 2+ flux. This emergent crowding effect, inaccessible to single‐additive strategies, enables unprecedented interfacial regulation. Electrochemical tests demonstrate ultrastable Zn plating/stripping over 1200 h at 5 mA cm −2 and 1800 h at 10 mA cm −2 , more than tenfold longer than the baseline electrolyte. This work establishes interfacial ion crowding as a powerful design principle, rooted in fundamental electrochemistry, offering a pathway toward high‐performance and durable AZMBs.
10.1002_anie.4470539: Rechargeable aqueous batteries are considered as promising energy storage devices due to their low cost and high safety. In rechargeable aqueous batteries, nonmetallic anodes have attracted widespread attention since they generally possess the characteristics of abundant resources, high designability, and dendrite-free. Although considerable research efforts have been made to design nonmetallic anodes, a comprehensive review about them is still absent. This review presents a systematic overview of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries, including conversion anodes and insertion anodes. Conversion-type anode materials primarily involve hydrogen gas, chalcogen compounds, and organic compounds, whereas intercalation-type anode materials focus on metal chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanionic compounds. In addition, their design principles are critically discussed with emphasis on energy storage mechanisms, merits and limitations, as well as compatibility with charge carriers and cathodes. In the final section, future developments and prospects in the design of high-performance nonmetallic anodes for aqueous batteries are also discussed. It will shed light on the R&D of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries.
